en: Points of Controversy The Great Fifty-Section The Fourteenth Chapter
The Discourse on the Arising of the Six Sense Bases:
Is it the case that the six sense bases are established in the mother’s womb neither before nor after [the other]?
Yes, it is.
“Does one possessing all limbs and members, with unimpaired faculties, descend into the mother’s womb?
One should not say so… [as before] … “Is the eye-base established by means of a rebirth-linking consciousness? One should not say so.
“Yes,” [you say].

“By means of the rebirth-linking consciousness, do the hands take shape, the feet take shape, the head takes shape, the ears take shape, the nose takes shape, the mouth takes shape, and the teeth take shape?
You should not speak thus… [and so on]…
Does the ear-base, the nose-base, and the tongue-base arise by means of a mind that is subject to rebirth?
“Yes,” [you say].

“By means of the mind belonging to rebirth, do the hands take shape, the feet take shape, the head takes shape, the ears take shape, the nose takes shape, the mouth takes shape, and the teeth take shape?
You should not speak thus… [and so on]… No, indeed.
Is it the case that the eye-base arises later for one who has entered the mother’s womb?
Yes. Does one perform kamma in the mother’s womb for the sake of obtaining the eye? No.
It should not be stated thus … [as before] … for one who has entered the mother’s womb,
the ear-base arises later … the nose-base arises later … [and so on].
Does the sense-base of the tongue arise?
Yes. Does one perform karma for the sake of obtaining the tongue in the mother’s womb? Yes.
It should not be said thus … [as before] … Is it the case that for one who has entered the mother’s womb,
the head-hairs, body-hairs, nails, teeth, and bones arise later?
Yes, it is.
Does one perform karma for the sake of obtaining bones within the mother’s womb?
One should not say so… [as before]… It should not be said.
“Do the head-hairs, body-hairs, nails, teeth, and bones arise later for one who has entered the mother’s womb?”—
“Yes.
But was it not said by the Blessed One:
“First there is the kalala;
from the kalala comes the abbuda;
from the abbuda the pesi is born.”
From the *peśī* the *ghana* is produced;
from the *ghana* the limbs arise,
as do the hair of the head, body hair, and nails.
Whatever food, drink, and sustenance his mother eats,
by that he maintains himself there.
“A man who has entered his mother’s womb”—
is this indeed a sutta?
Yes, it is.
Therefore, it is after one has entered the mother’s womb that the head-hairs, body-hairs, nails, teeth, and bones arise.
The discussion on the arising of the six sense bases is finished.
